intro_html: Real Goan vindaloo is not a heat contest. The name comes from the Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos, meaning meat in wine and garlic, and the dish that grew out of it in Goa swapped the wine for vinegar and added chilies. Sour, garlicky, deeply spiced pork over rice. It carries 36 grams of protein for about $4.66 a bowl (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $4.66 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a braise that takes an afternoon and tastes better every day it sits. Vindaloo was designed as a preserved dish, which is why the vinegar makes it hold so well in the fridge.
shop_smart: The spice paste is almost entirely jars you own. Cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, cinnamon and chili powder are pantry items, and buying them whole and grinding them yourself is cheaper still.
Dried arbol chiles cost pennies and last forever. A small bag sits in the cupboard for a year and gives you real chile flavor instead of just heat from a powder.
Skip the tamarind. Extra vinegar covers the sourness it would bring, and tamarind paste is a specialty purchase you would use twice.
Buy garlic by the head and buy a lot of it. This recipe uses an unusual amount, and garlic is the point of the dish, not a background note. Jarred garlic will not do here.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Soak the dried arbol chiles in hot water until they soften, then blend them with most of the garlic, the white vinegar, the cumin, coriander, garam masala, cinnamon, turmeric, chili powder and dijon mustard into a smooth paste.

Cut the pork shoulder into large cubes and coat it in the paste. Let it marinate at least an hour, and overnight in the fridge if you have the time. This is the step that makes it taste like vindaloo instead of curry.
Slice the onions and the jalapenos.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and cook the onions slowly until they go deep golden and sweet.
Add the marinated pork with all its paste and cook over medium heat, stirring, until the meat browns and the paste darkens and smells toasted rather than raw.
Add the diced tomatoes, the sliced jalapenos, the brown sugar, the bay leaves, salt and enough water to just cover, then bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and braise low until the pork shreds under a fork, then stir in the lime juice off the heat and cook the rice separately to serve underneath.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and ladle the exact amount over rice in each container, stirring the pot so the meat and sauce stay even. Every bowl lands near 710 calories and 36 grams of protein.

head.description: Goan pork vindaloo, a vinegar and garlic braise with a toasted chile spice paste, served over rice. 14 servings, 710 calories, 36g protein, about $4.66 each (at everyday cost).

steps: Soak the dried chiles, then blend them with garlic, vinegar and the ground spices into a paste.
Coat the cubed pork shoulder in the paste and marinate at least an hour.
Cook the sliced onions slowly in oil until deep golden.
Add the marinated pork and cook until browned and the paste darkens.
Add tomatoes, jalapenos, brown sugar and bay leaves, braise until the pork shreds, then finish with lime juice and serve over rice.
